report.finding: The model is fine and the integrator is fine. The ODE is dS1/dt = vo - k1*S1, a simple linear relaxation with time constant 1/k1 = 50 time units and steady state S1* = vo/k1 = 50. The user only simulated to t=10, i.e. 0.2 time constants, so S1 is still on the early, nearly-linear part of the exponential approach and naturally looks like it's "still climbing with no sign of levelling off." Tightening tolerances does nothing because there's no numerical error to fix - the trajectory is already accurate, it just hasn't gotten anywhere near equilibrium yet.
report.evidence: Analytic steady state: vo/k1 = 1/0.02 = 50, approach time constant 1/k1 = 50. Simulating rr.reset(); rr.simulate(0,300,300) gives S1(150)=47.5, S1(300)=49.9, consistent with exponential approach to 50 with tau=50. The original run only covered t=0..10 (0.2 tau), reaching S1=9.06, matching S1(t)=50*(1-exp(-0.02*10))=9.06 exactly - the solver is tracking the correct solution, the run is just far too short.

recommended_changes.why: With time constant 1/k1=50, the system needs several hundred time units to visibly approach its steady state of vo/k1=50; t=10 only reaches 18% of the way there.
